name: Paralegal
description: Paralegals do the substantive legal work that does not require a licence — drafting pleadings and contracts, investigating facts, searching records, managing discovery and keeping cases organised. ⚠ A median of $62,890 on an associate degree, at 32 Florida institutions. ⚠⚠⚠ Read the outlook honestly: this is the only path on this site where the federal handbook names ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE as a reason demand will be limited, and it projects 0% growth. That does not make it a bad career, but it changes how you should enter it.
credentialNote: ⚠ No licence is required and none exists. Anyone may work as a paralegal in Florida, and the BLS notes that some employers hire candidates with no legal education and train them on the job. ⚠⚠ What Florida offers instead is VOLUNTARY registration: the Florida Registered Paralegal programme, under Chapter 20 of the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar. The Bar is explicit that its criteria are above and beyond what is required to do paralegal work in Florida, and that you may continue working without registering. ⚠ Two routes qualify — education plus work experience, or NALA/NFPA certification plus work experience — and BOTH require an employing or supervising attorney to complete an attestation form, so you cannot self-certify. The fee is $145 to apply and $150 a year to renew. ⚠⚠ Maintaining it takes 30 hours of continuing education every three years, of which five must be ethics or professionalism and THREE MUST BE TECHNOLOGY. ⚠⚠⚠ Note that last requirement against the outlook section on this page: the profession's own regulator already treats technology competence as mandatory upkeep, which is the clearest signal available about where this job is going.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET, on paralegals and legal assistants: prepare affidavits or other documents, such as legal correspondence, and organize and maintain documents in paper or electronic filing system; prepare, edit, or review legal documents, including legislation, briefs, pleadings, appeals, wills, contracts, and real estate closing statements; investigate facts and law of cases and search pertinent sources, such as public records and internet sources.

⚠ A paralegal is not a legal secretary. The distinction is substantive legal work: research, drafting and factual investigation that a lawyer would otherwise do, performed under a lawyer's supervision and billed as legal work. It is also not a route into practising law — that requires a JD and the Bar examination, and this page's sibling covers it.

⚠⚠⚠ The outlook, stated plainly

RoleSOC2025 medianJobsOutlook 2025–35
Title examiner, abstractor and searcher23-2093$58,65057,4001–2% slower than average
Paralegal and legal assistant23-2011$62,890404,900⚠⚠ 0%, −1,100 jobs

And the BLS gives the reason, which it does for no other occupation on this site:

“Demand for these workers is expected to be limited by advances in technology, including artificial intelligence (AI). These technologies are expected to make paralegals and legal assistants more efficient at tasks such as conducting research and preparing documents, which may reduce demand for these workers.”

⚠⚠ Take that seriously and in proportion. Zero growth is not collapse — there are still 39,300 openings a year from people leaving and retiring, and 404,900 people doing this job. But the two tasks the handbook names as automatable — conducting research and preparing documents — are exactly the two tasks O*NET lists first. The core of the job is the part most exposed.

⚠⚠⚠ What survives is the part machines are worst at: interviewing a client who does not know which facts matter, tracking down a record that is not digitised, noticing that a document contradicts one filed two years ago, and managing a case through a court's procedures and deadlines. Enter this field aiming at that work, not at document production.

⚠⚠ Florida numbers this career twice, and it is a designed ladder

This is the clearest example on the site of a deliberate two-tier numbering scheme, and it will confuse you if nobody explains it. Florida's A.S. in Paralegal Studies is overwhelmingly a state-college credential using 1000- and 2000-level numbers; the BS in Legal Studies is a university credential using 3000- and 4000-level numbers — and it renumbers the same subjects.

SubjectState collegesUniversities
Family lawPLA 2800 — 18 institutionsPLA 3806 (2), PLA 4806 (2)
Law office managementPLA 2763 — 10PLA 4764 (2)
Property and real estatePLA 2610 — 12PLA 3613 (1)
BankruptcyPLA 2460 (2)PLA 3464 (1)

⚠ This is a DESIGN, not a defect. A baccalaureate requires upper-division hours, so the universities cannot count a 2000-level course toward one — hence the renumbering. The consequence for you is real all the same: if you complete the A.S. and then go on to the BS, expect to meet familiar subjects again at greater depth, and expect those credits to count as electives rather than as the requirement.

⚠⚠ Ask about Florida's excess-hours provisions before you enrol in the BS. Accumulating credits well beyond what a degree requires can carry a financial penalty, and the A.S.-then-BS route is exactly the shape that accumulates them. Get the articulation in writing from the receiving university, subject by subject.

⚠ And the state's own prerequisite data is unreliable here

Because the prefix splits by sector, the statewide prerequisite records — which are contributed by institutions — were written from the state-college side and name courses the universities do not carry.

  • PLA 4554 lists PLA 1003 and PLA 2203 as prerequisites. ⚠ UCF, which carries PLA 4554, carries neither — its real gate is freshman composition.
  • PLA 3806 lists PLA 1003. FGCU carries it; ⚠ UWF does not.

⚠⚠ So do not plan a sequence from the statewide record. Use your own institution's catalogue, and read a dangling prerequisite as a sign that the course belongs to the other tier rather than as something you have missed. The upside is worth noting: where the real gate turns out to be freshman composition, the course is open to students outside the major.

✅ What does travel

The state-college core is well carried and transfers within that tier: PLA 1003 Introduction to Paralegal Studies at 19 institutions, PLA 2800 Family Law at 18, PLA 1104 and PLA 2114 Legal Research and Writing at 16 each, PLA 2600 Wills, Trusts and Estates at 14, PLA 2610 Real Estate Law at 12, PLA 2273 Tort Law at 10.

⚠ One caution carried over from the wider catalogue: do not infer the level from the sector. St Petersburg College is a state college and carries PLA 4806 and PLA 4554 at 4000 level, because it holds baccalaureate authority. Check the carrier, not the institution type.

⚠ Registration is worth it, and later than you think

The Florida Registered Paralegal credential requires an attorney attestation under both eligibility routes, which means you cannot obtain it before you are employed. It is a mid-career marker rather than an entry ticket, and the same is true of the NALA and NFPA certifications that satisfy the alternative route.

⚠⚠ The continuing-education requirement is the interesting part. Thirty hours every three years, of which five must be ethics or professionalism and three must be technology. The Bar has already decided that technology competence is a permanent obligation of this profession — which is the most direct institutional answer available to the automation question above.

Necessary skills

  • Legal research and writing, to a standard a lawyer will sign. This is the core academic skill and the two courses that teach it are the most widely carried in the prefix.
  • Procedure and deadlines. Courts run on rules about time, and a missed deadline is a malpractice problem rather than an inconvenience.
  • Factual investigation. Finding the record, the witness or the inconsistency — the least automatable part of the work.
  • Document and discovery management at scale, increasingly with e-discovery and AI tools. Learn to run them rather than compete with them.
  • Absolute discretion. You will hold privileged information, and the privilege is the client's.
  • Knowing the line. A paralegal may not give legal advice or represent a client, and understanding exactly where that line falls is itself professional knowledge.

Advice

⚠⚠ Pick the tier deliberately. The A.S. at a state college is the cheapest route to the job and it is what most Florida paralegals hold. The BS is a different credential at a different level, and taking both means repeating subjects. If you know you want the bachelor's, ask whether going straight to it is cheaper than the ladder.

⚠ Aim at a specialism the automation does not reach. Litigation support, e-discovery management, trial preparation, complex real-estate closings and probate administration all involve judgement, clients and physical records. General document production is the part under pressure.

⚠ Become the person who runs the AI tools. The Bar mandates three hours of technology CE every cycle for registered paralegals. The firms are adopting these tools whatever you do, and the paralegal who configures and checks them is more valuable, not less.

⚠ Get registered once you are employed, and get your supervising attorney's attestation while you still work there — it is much harder to obtain after you leave.

And if law itself is the goal, read the Lawyer path first. Paralegal work is a genuinely good way to find out whether you like the profession before committing to a JD, and a great many law students did exactly that — but it is not a shortcut, and no part of it substitutes for the degree.

cipCodes.note: Law — included because this career sits directly beneath it, and because paralegal work is one of the commonest ways people test whether they want to go to law school. ⚠ It is not a route: no part of a paralegal credential substitutes for a JD.

⚠ Business administration — the BLS notes that employers preferring a bachelor's often hire candidates who majored in social science or BUSINESS and added a paralegal certificate. With 46 Florida public institutions, it is the most available degree that route can be built on.

programs.note: The programme itself — 32 Florida public institutions, weighted to the associate degree (320 of the state's credentials against 133 bachelor's). ⚠ Read this page's ladder section before choosing a tier: the A.S. and the BS renumber the same subjects, and taking both means repeating them.

⚠ Not a route from here — a JD requires a bachelor's degree and the law school admission process, and no paralegal credential shortens it. ⚠⚠ Named because paralegal work is one of the best available ways to find out whether you actually want the profession before committing three years and the cost, and because many law students came this way.

⚠ A real alternative route to the same job: the federal handbook describes employers who prefer a bachelor's hiring graduates who majored in business or a social science and added a paralegal certificate. ⚠⚠ Available at 46 Florida public institutions against 32 teaching paralegal studies, so for many students it is the more practical base.

courses.reason: Introduction to Paralegal Studies — 19 institutions, the most widely carried course in the prefix and the gateway to every Florida A.S. in this field. The role, its ethical limits, and the structure of the legal system.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Carried entirely by state colleges. Several universities name it as a prerequisite for their upper-division courses without carrying it themselves — see this page's note on dangling prerequisites.

courses.reason: Legal Research and Writing I — 16 institutions. ⚠ The core academic skill of the profession: finding authority and writing it up to a standard a lawyer will sign.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ The single most important course in this list, and the one least threatened by automation — AI drafts, and somebody has to know whether what it drafted is right.

courses.reason: Legal Research and Writing II — 16 institutions. The second half: longer documents, more complex authority, and citation done properly.
Civil Procedure I — 8 institutions. The rules that govern how a case moves: pleadings, service, motions and deadlines. Procedure is where paralegals add the most and where mistakes cost the most.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Named as a prerequisite by the statewide record for PLA4554, which UCF carries — and UCF does not carry this course. ⚠ Read that as evidence of the sector split, not as something you have missed.

courses.reason: Civil Procedure II — 8 institutions. Discovery, depositions, pre-trial practice and trial support, which is where litigation paralegals spend their working lives.
Family Law — 18 institutions, the second most widely carried course in the prefix. Dissolution, custody, support and the Florida statutes and forms that govern them.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ The clearest example of the ladder: the universities renumber this as PLA3806 (FGCU, UWF) or PLA4806 (St Petersburg, UCF), each at 2 institutions. Same subject, upper division, and a 2000-level course cannot supply upper-division hours toward a bachelor's.

courses.reason: Wills, Trusts and Estates — 14 institutions. Probate administration is one of the specialisms where paralegals do the most independent work, and Florida's demographics guarantee the volume.
Real Estate Law — 12 institutions. Closings, title and conveyancing, which in Florida is a large and durable employer of paralegals.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Renumbered by the universities as PLA3613 Property Law and Transactions (UWF). ⚠⚠ This subject also connects to the title examiner role covered on this page — different job, same records.

courses.reason: Tort Law — 10 institutions. Negligence and personal injury: the substantive law behind a large share of Florida civil litigation.
Law Office Management — 10 institutions. Billing, trust accounting, file management and the technology a firm actually runs on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Renumbered by the universities as PLA4764 Law Office Practices (UCF, UWF). ⚠⚠ More useful than it sounds: trust accounting errors are a Bar discipline matter, and the paralegal often maintains the records.

courses.reason: Contracts — 2 institutions under this number. Formation, performance and breach — the substantive law behind most transactional work.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Thinly carried in the paralegal prefix because most students meet contracts through BUL2241 Business Law I (25 institutions) instead. Either serves.

courses.reason: Environmental Law — 2 institutions (St Petersburg College, UCF), upper division. Included as the worked example of both the ladder and the dangling-prerequisite problem.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Its statewide prerequisites name PLA1003 and PLA2203, and UCF carries NEITHER — its real gate is freshman composition. ⚠ Note also that St Petersburg is a STATE COLLEGE carrying a 4000-level course, because it holds baccalaureate authority: do not infer the level from the sector.

courses.reason: Business Law I — 25 institutions. Contracts, agency and commercial law, widely carried and a good substitute where the paralegal prefix does not carry a contracts course.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. ⚠ More load-bearing here than on most paths: it is the actual prerequisite for some upper-division paralegal courses, and the whole job is writing.
Computer Applications for Business — 14 institutions. Document management, spreadsheets and databases — and the base the e-discovery and AI tooling sits on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Worth more than it looks given the outlook on this page: the Florida Bar requires registered paralegals to take three hours of TECHNOLOGY continuing education every cycle. Technology competence is treated as permanent professional upkeep in this field.
